t-distribution.def: A family of symmetric, bell-shaped density curves centered at 0, with heavier tails than the standard normal. Each is set by its degrees of freedom; as df grows, the t distribution approaches the standard normal. Its critical values are written $t^*$.

one-sample-t-interval.def: A confidence interval for a population mean when $\sigma$ is unknown: $\bar{x} \pm t^*\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$, with $\text{df} = n - 1$. Conditions: random, 10%, normal/large sample.

paired-data.def: Two measurements that belong together, on the same individual or on two matched individuals (before and after, left and right, twins). Analyze the differences as one sample; the parameter is the true mean difference $\mu_d$.

normal-large-sample.def: The shape condition for t procedures: the population is normal, or the sample size is at least 30, or a graph of the sample data (dotplot, boxplot, histogram) shows no strong skew and no outliers.
